title: Real-time imaging of membrane fission by mitofissin
author: Maruyama, Noda.

steps.title: Transform and grow E. coli
steps.instruction: Transform competent E. coli C41(DE3) cells with the in‑house modified pET15b‑SpAtg44 plasmid. Inoculate the transformants into 10 mL LB medium containing 100 mg/L ampicillin in a 50‑mL plastic tube and grow at 37 °C for ~16 h. Transfer the culture to 1 L LB +100 mg/L ampicillin in a 2‑L baffled flask, grow at 37 °C until OD600≈0.8, induce protein expression by adding IPTG from a 0.5 M stock to a final concentration of 0.5 mM, then incubate at 20 °C for ~20 h. Harvest cells by centrifugation at 4,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend cells and add protease inhibitor
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 35 mL phosphate buffer. The suspension may be stored at –80 °C. Add phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF) from a 0.1 M ethanol stock to a final concentration of 1.0 mM.

steps.title: Lyse cells by sonication
steps.instruction: Lyse the cells on ice using a tip sonicator (500 W, 20 kHz) with the tube immersed in ice water. Sonicate at 50 % amplitude in 1‑s bursts followed by 4‑s rests for a total of 15 min.

steps.title: Clarify lysate and bind to amylose resin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 38,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C. Load the supernatant onto ~3 mL amylose resin pre‑equilibrated with phosphate buffer in a 20‑mL gravity column without disturbing the resin. Wash the resin with 40 mL phosphate buffer (high salt >1 M NaCl is essential for homogeneous purification).

steps.title: Elute and cleave MBP tag
steps.instruction: Elute bound protein with 10 mL phosphate buffer supplemented with 10 mM maltose. Add homemade (or commercial Cytiva) PreScission protease to a final concentration of ~1 µM and incubate at 4 °C for ~16 h to remove the MBP tag.

steps.title: Check MBP cleavage by SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run a 15 % polyacrylamide SDS‑PAGE and stain with Coomassie blue G‑250 to verify MBP cleavage.

steps.title: Ni‑NTA affinity purification
steps.instruction: Load the protease‑treated sample onto ~3 mL Ni‑NTA resin pre‑equilibrated with phosphate buffer in a 20‑mL gravity column (SpAtg44 binds Ni‑NTA without a His‑tag). Wash the resin with 30 mL HEPES buffer containing 10 mM imidazole. Elute the protein with 10 mL HEPES buffer supplemented with 200 mM imidazole.

steps.title: Buffer exchange, concentrate and aliquot
steps.instruction: Assess purity by SDS‑PAGE (Coomassie stain). Concentrate the eluate to ~250 µL using a 10‑kDa centrifugal filter at 4 °C. Add 10 mL HEPES buffer to the concentrate and reconcentrate; repeat this buffer‑exchange cycle three times total. Divide the purified SpAtg44 into small aliquots and freeze at –80 °C (≈10 mg/L culture can be obtained). Avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles; size‑exclusion chromatography is optional.

steps.title: Prepare liposome stock
steps.instruction: In a 5‑mL glass vial, combine the desired lipids (total 100 nmol) using glass syringes. Dry the chloroform under a gentle stream of nitrogen while rotating the vial to form a thin film, then place the vial in a desiccator connected to a rotary pump for >12 h to remove residual solvent. Add 400 µL water to the film, vortex to suspend, transfer to a 1.5‑mL plastic tube, and sonicate with a handheld tip sonicator at ~40 % output power in 10‑s bursts with 10‑s rests until the solution becomes transparent. Centrifuge at 18,000 × g for 15 min at 25 °C, and transfer the supernatant (liposome solution) to a fresh tube. Prepare liposomes immediately before use.

steps.title: Prepare excess membrane reservoirs
steps.instruction: To 160 µL liposome solution (250 µM total lipids) add 40 µL of 5.0 M NaCl. Add 20 µL silica‑bead suspension (pre‑vortexed) and vortex intermittently for 30 min at 20‑25 °C. Add 780 µL water, centrifuge at 500 × g for 1 min at 25 °C, and carefully remove ~950 µL supernatant without disturbing the bead pellet. Resuspend the pellet with ~950 µL water, centrifuge again under the same conditions, and repeat the wash (remove supernatant, resuspend) three times total to eliminate unbound liposomes. Finally, remove ~950 µL supernatant, leaving the bead pellet that constitutes the excess membrane reservoirs (use freshly prepared reservoirs for efficient nanotube formation).

steps.title: Assemble observation chamber
steps.instruction: Assemble a chamber using a C‑shaped silicone rubber spacer sandwiched between a cover glass and a glass slide. Fill the chamber with HEPES buffer containing 1 mg/mL BSA at 20‑25 °C, then immediately remove the BSA solution (prolonged incubation reduces nanotube yield). Re‑fill the chamber with HEPES buffer.

steps.title: Generate lipid nanotubes
steps.instruction: Aspirate the excess‑membrane‑reservoir suspension and deposit it at the open side of the observation chamber. Tilt the chamber >20° so the reservoirs roll slowly over the bottom toward the interior. Continue tilting until the reservoirs reach the inner wall, then place the chamber horizontally. Immediately place the chamber on the stage of a confocal laser‑scanning microscope to observe the fluorescent lipid nanotubes (use within 1 h of preparation).

description: The protocol below provides a comprehensive guide to conducting in vitro membrane fission observation using Atg44 as an example. This protocol uses lipid nanotubes as model membranes. The nanotubes can be prepared by the interaction between lipids and glass surface without requiring special or expensive devices. The lipid composition of the nanotubes is intentionally designed to mimic that of the inner mitochondrial membrane, ensuring relevance to the intermembrane space where Atg44 is located. However, the lipid composition can be adjusted to suit the research interests. Notably, we have successfully generated lipid nanotubes using various lipid compositions such as 1:1 of phosphatidylcholine (PC) and phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), 2:1:1 of PC, PE and an acidic phospholipid like phosphatidylinositol (PI), implying the flexibility of this protocol. Moreover, this protocol can be modified and applied to assess the fission activity of other proteins. Sample preparation, appropriate lipid composition selection, and necessary cofactor identification relevant to membrane fission observation mediated by the protein of interest should be carefully considered before starting the protocol. Appropriate starting lipid composition can be studied using a liposome flotation assay that reveals the binding of the protein of your interest to the lipid membranes.
